nodes.label: Attention-precision hypothesis (555-99 is a capacity limit, not a data gap)
nodes.norm_label: attention-precision hypothesis (555-99 is a capacity limit, not a data gap)
nodes.rationale: The digit drop survived 1,200 targeted examples, so data could not fix it — evidence that the bug is an attention-precision limit. Framed explicitly as a falsifiable prediction that Phase 8's scale experiment was built to test.

nodes.label: Digit-drop failure: 555-99 read as 55 - 99 = 4
nodes.rationale: Diagnosed from a real chat screenshot as an operand misread: training only had 3-digit x 3-digit and mostly spaced operands. 1,200 targeted mixed_digit examples did NOT fix it, which reframed the diagnosis from a data gap to an attention-precision limit.

nodes.label: Multi-turn conversation training (2,500 blocks: convo_math, convo_facts, convo_correct, convo_chat)
nodes.norm_label: multi-turn conversation training (2,500 blocks: convo_math, convo_facts, convo_correct, convo_chat)
nodes.rationale: Each block is one training example containing several Q/A turns, teaching follow-ups that resolve against the previous answer, elliptical questions ('and Japan?'), corrections, and non-question statements — the one capability Aizen had never had.

nodes.label: Not-a-question failure: the correction 'cats can't bark' -> 'Aw, 2 dogs can bark.'
nodes.norm_label: not-a-question failure: the correction 'cats can't bark' -> 'aw, 2 dogs can bark.'
nodes.rationale: Zero dialogue training meant plain statements broke the model; addressed by convo_chat and convo_correct multi-turn blocks that train statements and gracefully acknowledged corrections.

nodes.label: server.py history packing (last 6 turns within the context budget)
nodes.norm_label: server.py history packing (last 6 turns within the context budget)
nodes.rationale: server.py accepts a history array and packs recent turns into the prompt within the 512-token context budget; the UI sends the last 6 turns, which is what bounds conversation depth to ~6 turns.

nodes.label: data/eval.json (400 questions, 8 categories)
nodes.rationale: 50 questions per category generated deterministically by make_eval_data.py at seed 4242. Near-zero baselines on logic/patterns/instruction/reading/coding are intentional — those are the numbers later phases are meant to move.

nodes.label: Phase 2 reasoning + instruction dataset (10,000 examples)
nodes.rationale: 5,000 instruction + 5,000 reasoning records generated deterministically at seed 20260827, 100% compatible with the 73-char vocab and capped at 190 rendered chars to fit the 192-char context.

nodes.label: validate_phase2_data.py independent recomputation
nodes.rationale: Recomputes counts, ids, vocab compliance, render length, leakage checks, every equation in every reasoning chain and per-category answers independently of the generator, exiting non-zero on any failure — a second opinion rather than a self-check.

nodes.label: Per-category noise floor (~7pp at n=50)
nodes.rationale: With 50 questions per category, small deltas between checkpoints are inside the noise band and must not be read as real improvement; single-sample deterministic scoring measures one fixed draw, not the output distribution.

nodes.label: Whitelisted arithmetic skeletons (324 examples)
nodes.rationale: Approved policy exception: 324 examples share an eval arithmetic template shape with guaranteed-disjoint numbers, because number-generalization is exactly the skill being tested. All other eval templates are fully blocked.

nodes.label: Python-computed deterministic answers and chains
nodes.rationale: All arithmetic, sorting, counting, reversing, case and pattern answers are computed by Python and never guessed, and reasoning chains are constructed from the computation so every intermediate equation is true by construction.

nodes.label: Eval leakage controls and disjoint vocabulary
nodes.norm_label: eval leakage controls and disjoint vocabulary
nodes.rationale: Exact, digit-masked-template and operand-tuple matches with eval questions are rejected during generation, and names/objects/colors are deliberately disjoint from the eval set's so any transfer measured is generalization rather than memorization.

nodes.norm_label: patterns_v3 — sequences rebuilt for the bpe representation

nodes.label: Synthetic Q&A Dataset (qa.txt)
nodes.rationale: 25,390 Q&A pairs (~0.97MB) generated deterministically by make_qa_data.py (seed 1337): small talk, country capitals, general facts, and arithmetic (add/sub/mul). Each fact appears under multiple phrasings so the model learns patterns rather than memorized strings.

nodes.label: Frozen 400-question evaluation harness (eval.py)
nodes.rationale: Exists because every earlier claim rested on ad-hoc manual spot checks, making it impossible to tell whether a change actually improved the model or just felt better. It is the fixed before/after photo for every later phase, scored identically every time.

nodes.label: Category-appropriate scoring checkers
nodes.rationale: number (last number must match), contains (word-boundary aware substring), yes_no (exactly one of yes/no), one_word_correct, three_items (count only). No generated code is ever executed; unencodable questions are flagged and counted incorrect.

nodes.label: Capacity Ceiling — the Shared Cause Behind Every Earlier Trade-Off
nodes.norm_label: capacity ceiling — the shared cause behind every earlier trade-off

nodes.label: Reproducible per-question seeding (1337 + index)
nodes.rationale: Seeding torch before each question makes two runs give identical answers and identical scores while keeping the normal sampling configuration — determinism without switching to greedy decoding.

nodes.label: Inline reasoning-on-answer-line format
nodes.rationale: Chosen over a separate 'T:' chain-of-thought line because every existing inference path (frozen eval.py, chat.py, server.py) prompts 'Q: ...\nA:' and stops at the first newline — a T: line would never be generated at eval time. Inline lets the model emit chain and answer in one line and the frozen last-number checker scores it with zero changes; the JSON keeps reasoning as a separate field for other renderings later.

nodes.label: Chain-format overgeneralization (arithmetic regression)
nodes.rationale: Arithmetic fell 78% -> 72% because single-step subtraction phrased 'How much is 67 - 53?' now triggers the two-step chain template, and the model adds first since most training chains start with addition. 6 of the 11 broken questions are exactly this.

nodes.label: Phase 3 recommended next experiments
nodes.rationale: Short term: fix the subtraction regression and logic/reading transfer with data (single-step chain-format examples, many more deduction phrasings, far greater name/object variety) — costs nothing but generation time. Longer term: from-scratch BPE tokenizer, then pretraining on quality text within the 50M-param budget.

nodes.label: Checkpoint-carried tokenizer auto-detection in eval.py
nodes.rationale: eval.py received tokenizer plumbing only: encode/decode/stop come from the checkpoint (BPE or legacy char, auto-detected) while questions, sampling parameters and scoring stayed untouched, and the legacy path was re-verified on v1b — so v0/v1/v1b/v2 scores remain comparable.

nodes.label: Every digit is its own token
nodes.norm_label: every digit is its own token
nodes.rationale: '123' is always three tokens because multi-digit tokens would make arithmetic unlearnable at this scale.

nodes.label: Patterns regression 14 -> 4 under BPE
nodes.rationale: Number sequences now tokenize as digit pieces inside a comma layout the model saw only ~500 examples of — too few for the new representation, so it emits arithmetic-shaped noise. Honestly reported: BPE changed which skills are cheap to learn.

nodes.label: Deliberate eval dip: v4b 52.25 -> v5 48.0 (patterns 34->14, reading 48->38)
nodes.norm_label: deliberate eval dip: v4b 52.25 -> v5 48.0 (patterns 34->14, reading 48->38)
nodes.rationale: A deliberate trade of -4.25 benchmark points for a capability the benchmark cannot measure: the frozen eval has no multi-turn category, so it sees only what conversation training cost. Reported as the honest headline rather than hidden.

nodes.label: Dual-checkpoint policy: v4b served the eval, v5 served the chat UI
nodes.norm_label: dual-checkpoint policy: v4b served the eval, v5 served the chat ui
nodes.rationale: Both checkpoints were kept because they optimize different things — v4b remained the eval champion while v5 carried the conversational capability the eval cannot score.

nodes.label: Eval blind spot: the frozen eval has no multi-turn category
nodes.norm_label: eval blind spot: the frozen eval has no multi-turn category
nodes.rationale: The benchmark cannot score conversation, so the phase's actual gain was verified by direct probes instead; a multi-turn category would be needed to measure it. Corrections are also acknowledged rather than genuinely integrated.

nodes.label: Negatives failure: 2+4-9 produced nonsense
nodes.rationale: Every training result had been >= 0, so the model had never seen a minus sign as an answer; fixed with an 800-example negatives slice whose reasoning explains why the result is below zero. Verified afterwards: '2 + 4 = 6. Then, 6 - 9 = -3.'

nodes.label: Limitation: One Run, One Seed — ~7pp Per-Category Noise Floor at n=50
nodes.norm_label: limitation: one run, one seed — ~7pp per-category noise floor at n=50

nodes.label: Finding: the See-Saw Ends — Every Category Simultaneously at an All-Time High
nodes.norm_label: finding: the see-saw ends — every category simultaneously at an all-time high

nodes.label: Phase 3 fine-tune (v1, aizen_phase3.pt)
nodes.rationale: Fine-tunes v0 on the Phase 2 dataset mixed with qa.txt to improve instruction following, multi-step reasoning, logic, patterns and reading while preserving arithmetic, knowledge and conversation — judged solely by the frozen eval. Result: 17.0% -> 26.5%, 49 fixed / 11 broken.

nodes.label: From-scratch BPE tokenizer (tokenizer.py)
nodes.rationale: Written from scratch with stdlib only (no tiktoken/HF/sentencepiece), GPT-2-style word-level merging where a regex pre-splits text so merges never cross word boundaries and leading spaces attach to words. Trained on qa.txt + phase3b text only, with eval.json excluded. Final vocab 2048 = 4 specials + 96 base chars + 1948 merges.

nodes.label: 2.19x corpus compression
nodes.rationale: 2,705,595 char tokens become 1,234,733 BPE tokens (3.99 -> 1.82 tokens/word), which is what makes a 512-token context worth ~1,121 chars — 5.8x the old window.

nodes.label: Special tokens (<pad>/<unk>/<bos>/<eos>)
nodes.rationale: Deterministic ids 0-3; <unk> safely replaces non-ASCII input (documented lossy decode) and the base vocab includes all printable ASCII, so characters like X ( ) % # " that crashed the old tokenizer now encode and round-trip exactly. <pad>/<bos>/<eos> reserved but unused this phase.

nodes.label: Per-category interpretation rules
nodes.rationale: Compare per-category rather than overall: a reasoning phase should move multi-step/logic while leaving general_knowledge alone. Fluent-but-wrong knowledge answers indicate template memorization without question understanding; right-content-wrong-format instruction failures are exactly what instruction tuning fixes.

nodes.label: Catastrophic forgetting warning (mix with qa.txt)
nodes.rationale: Training on the Phase 2 file alone would destroy Phase-0 skills, so Phase 3 is required to train on a mixture of this dataset and data/qa.txt.

nodes.label: Answer-only loss masking
nodes.rationale: Loss is computed only on target characters after '\nA:' through the terminating newline (newline included so the model learns to stop); question text and scaffolding contribute zero loss. Consequence: these masked losses are not comparable with train_qa.py's unmasked losses.

nodes.label: 70/30 qa.txt + Phase 2 window mixture
nodes.rationale: 70% of windows packed from qa.txt and 30% from the Phase 2 text (about 47/53 by characters since Phase 2 examples are ~2.6x longer); the mixture is what protected old knowledge — general knowledge went up rather than down.

nodes.label: Example-aligned training windows
nodes.rationale: Every window starts at a 'Q:' and only the last example per window is cut, so position 0 always aligns with a question start — matching the shape of inference prompts.

nodes.label: Template-binding failure (format learned, function not)
nodes.rationale: Logic stayed at 0% and reading at 4% because the model produces memorized deduction-shaped answers about the wrong entities and retrieves memorized passages instead of reading the prompt: it learned the deduction FORMAT, not the deduction FUNCTION. Diagnosis: at 14M params char-level, the model generalizes across numbers well but across wording poorly — template diversity per skill matters more than examples per template.

nodes.label: Documented Phase 4 deviations (lr 3e-4, 3b data included)
nodes.rationale: Learning rate raised from the specified 1e-4 to 3e-4 because this is scratch training rather than a fine-tune, and the 3b fixes were kept in the new-data pool because excluding them would conflate the tokenizer effect with a data downgrade. Both disclosed rather than silently applied.

nodes.label: Full scratch re-initialization for v2
nodes.rationale: Justified because the vocab change invalidates embedding and head, token granularity changes every layer's input statistics, and the positional table cannot be extended 192 -> 512; partial transfer would confound the tokenizer experiment.

nodes.label: Newline never merges
nodes.rationale: '\n' is excluded from merges because it terminates answers and generation stops on it — merging it into another token would break the stop condition.

nodes.label: Train/inference tokenization parity
nodes.rationale: The prompt part and answer part of each training example are tokenized separately so training prompt tokenization is byte-identical to inference tokenization.

nodes.label: Multi-turn answer-turn loss masking (parse_examples masks every A: line)
nodes.norm_label: multi-turn answer-turn loss masking (parse_examples masks every a: line)
nodes.rationale: Extends the single-turn answer-masked loss so all answer turns in a block train, not just the first. Chosen because it is token-identical to the old parser on single-turn data — the newline is a standalone token that never merges — so no earlier behaviour changes.

nodes.label: False-premise failure: 'if aizen is cat then can aizen bark?' -> 'all cats can bark... yes'
nodes.norm_label: false-premise failure: 'if aizen is cat then can aizen bark?' -> 'all cats can bark... yes'
nodes.rationale: Training always supplied a true premise, so given none the model invented one. Fixed with 700 false_premise examples where the model must supply the true fact ('A cat cannot bark. A cat can meow.') before answering.

nodes.label: Aizen architecture — decoder-only Transformer, GPT-2 layout
nodes.norm_label: aizen architecture — decoder-only transformer, gpt-2 layout
nodes.rationale: ~150 commented lines; x + Attention(LN(x)) then x + MLP(LN(x)), causal scaled dot-product attention, learned absolute positions, weight-tied head. Unmodified since Phase 0 except the class name — config numbers alone took it from 14M to 40M, because the interesting decisions live in data and method, not architecture.

nodes.label: Repository file map
nodes.rationale: Groups the codebase into model/inference, evaluation, training, data generation and documentation so a reader can find the load-bearing files.

nodes.label: Vaswani et al., 'Attention Is All You Need' (2017)
nodes.norm_label: vaswani et al., 'attention is all you need' (2017)

nodes.label: Chunked, resumable training with per-chunk reseeding
nodes.norm_label: chunked, resumable training with per-chunk reseeding
nodes.rationale: Seed 1337 throughout, CHUNK_ITERS default 250 so a laptop can close its lid mid-run; the sampler must be re-seeded per chunk.

nodes.label: Honest limitations
nodes.rationale: Coding at 2% (no code in TinyStories), thin knowledge at 64% general knowledge with no notion of 'I don't know', three-digit arithmetic still slipping, a synthetic self-authored benchmark not comparable to MMLU, missing batch-size metadata and NaN final_masked_* fields, and 40M parameters against the ~10,000x more a general assistant needs.

nodes.label: Silent Metal GPU memory corruption
nodes.rationale: At 40M parameters, MPS batch sizes above ~20 produced NaN gradients instead of an OOM error because Metal zeroed gradients rather than raising; found by bisection and fixed with batch 12 x accumulation 2 plus a non-finite gradient-norm guard.

nodes.label: PyTorch with the MPS backend
nodes.rationale: The only runtime dependency besides Flask for the server.

nodes.label: The per-chunk reseeding bug
nodes.rationale: Live from Phase 3 through Phase 8: each resumed chunk re-seeded the sampler identically and redrew the same batches, so the model saw a slice of its corpus repeatedly. Its fingerprint is a train/val divergence (0.95 gap with the bug, 0.01 without). Fixed in three lines by re-seeding from args.seed + 7919 * start_iter.

nodes.label: Stage 1 — TinyStories pretraining (16,000 steps)
nodes.rationale: From scratch, batch 12 x 512 with grad accumulation 2, ~196.6M tokens processed (~3.7 epochs over 52.5M unique), LR 3e-4 cosine -> 3e-5 AdamW; final train 1.367 / val 1.356.

nodes.label: Aizen Storyteller (aizen_phase8_pretrained.pt)
nodes.rationale: The identical weights before fine-tuning, kept as a shippable sibling so the pure-TinyStories language model stays inspectable.

nodes.label: TinyStories pretraining corpus
nodes.rationale: Synthetic stories with a ~1,500-word vocabulary chosen because a small model can actually fit the distribution; cleaned to printable ASCII so story and task data share one alphabet, with story start offsets kept so windows align to story boundaries.

nodes.label: Two-stage training pipeline
nodes.rationale: Stage 1 plain next-token prediction on TinyStories, stage 2 answer-masked loss on the task mixture; both stages share tokenizer and config so weights transfer 1:1.

nodes.label: Aizen v6 (aizen_phase8.pt, 40,188,928 params, 60.75%)
nodes.rationale: Current release: 12 layers / 512 dim / 8 heads, 512 context, 4,096 BPE vocab, trained on one MacBook Air with PyTorch MPS.

nodes.label: The Phase 5 corpus — a 103MB TinyStories slice
nodes.norm_label: the phase 5 corpus — a 103mb tinystories slice
nodes.rationale: Chosen because small models can fit its ~1,500-word distribution; cleaned to printable ASCII to share the tokenizer's alphabet with task data, 26,161,910 tokens over 116,509 stories.

nodes.label: Phase 5 limitations
nodes.rationale: Coding untouched at 2% because TinyStories has no code; TinyStories teaches sentence structure and implication rather than world knowledge (general knowledge moved only 48 -> 58); stage 2 was under-budgeted; and the reseeding bug affects every number in the document.

nodes.label: Logic 12% -> 66% — the largest single-category jump in the project
nodes.norm_label: logic 12% -> 66% — the largest single-category jump in the project
nodes.rationale: It came with zero new logic training data: the Phase 3b pool was unchanged and only the initialisation differed. The model could not do 'all cats are animals, Whiskers is a cat, therefore...' because it had never read a sentence carrying an implication.

nodes.label: Hindsight limitation — the reseeding bug invalidates the stage-1 numbers
nodes.norm_label: hindsight limitation — the reseeding bug invalidates the stage-1 numbers
nodes.rationale: The 0.95 train/val gap is not ordinary overfitting on 26M tokens of a low-entropy corpus but the reseeding bug's fingerprint, so v3's 45.25% was achieved on an unmeasured fraction of 26.2M tokens. It strengthens the conclusion (pretraining bought 54 points of logic while handicapped) but means Phase 5 and Phase 8 are not a clean comparison of scale.

nodes.label: Phase 5 stage 1 — 16M-parameter pretraining
nodes.rationale: From scratch with no task weights (the point is to learn language first): 8 layers, 384 dim, 6 heads, 512 context, 15,965,952 params, 16,000 steps at batch 32, plain next-token cross-entropy with every token a target; loss 8.364 -> train 1.042 / val 1.994.

nodes.label: Story-boundary-aligned training windows
nodes.rationale: Story start offsets are stored so a training window begins at a story rather than mid-sentence.

nodes.label: The two-stage split — Aizen becomes a pipeline
nodes.norm_label: the two-stage split — aizen becomes a pipeline
nodes.rationale: Both stages share one tokenizer and one config so stage 2 loads stage 1's weights 1:1; this is genuine fine-tuning, not a re-initialisation.

nodes.label: Known limits
nodes.rationale: Coding at 2% with no code in the corpus, three-digit arithmetic slipping, Phase 8 confounded by scale and sampler fix landing together, and 40M parameters meaning it is a demonstration of method rather than a source of facts.

nodes.label: Resumable chunked training
nodes.rationale: Each call trains CHUNK_ITERS steps, writes checkpoints/<tag>_resume.pt and picks up where it stopped; without per-chunk sampler re-seeding every resumed chunk redraws identical batches and the run silently trains on a fraction of its data.

nodes.label: Phase 8 is confounded
nodes.rationale: The scale increase and the reseeding fix landed in the same run, so '40M parameters caused +12.75 points' is not a supportable claim; separating them needs a 16M-with-fixed-sampler ablation that was never run.

nodes.label: Pretraining is not a scale trick
nodes.norm_label: pretraining is not a scale trick
nodes.rationale: At a fixed 16M parameters, reading TinyStories moved logic from 12% to 66% with zero new logic training data.

nodes.label: Capability and knowledge are separable
nodes.rationale: Task data teaches what shape the answer takes; it cannot teach the reasoning the answer requires if there is no language model underneath. At a fixed 16M parameters pretraining bought 9.5 points overall and 54 points of logic.

nodes.label: Frozen 400-question benchmark
nodes.rationale: 8 categories, 50 questions each, written before any improvement work and never edited; scoring is deterministic under torch.manual_seed(1337 + i) and auto-detects char-level vs BPE checkpoints so every generation is scored by identical code.

nodes.label: Benchmark progression v0 -> v6 across 8 categories
nodes.norm_label: benchmark progression v0 -> v6 across 8 categories
nodes.rationale: 400 questions, 50 per category, written before any improvement work and never edited; v6 is the first generation where every category is simultaneously at its all-time high.

nodes.label: Build-your-own recipe
nodes.rationale: Write and freeze the benchmark first, then architecture, then a tokenizer respecting the task's structure, pretrain on prose before fine-tuning on tasks, fine-tune with answer-only loss at a lower LR, diagnose the failure mode rather than the score, and write down what a change costs.

nodes.label: Two standing evaluation rules
nodes.rationale: Questions are never modified and never tuned against; one training run per approved experiment, with no quiet retries and no picking the best of several seeds.

nodes.label: Eval leakage control
nodes.rationale: The 400 eval questions were generated first and every later generator rejects collisions against data/eval.json — Phase 6 rejected 243 candidates; validation reports 0 false equations and 0 eval leaks.

nodes.label: Noise floor of roughly +/-7 points at n=50
nodes.norm_label: noise floor of roughly +/-7 points at n=50
nodes.rationale: Single-category moves smaller than the noise floor are not evidence of anything.

nodes.label: The v1-v5 see-saw was a capacity ceiling, not a data problem
nodes.norm_label: the v1-v5 see-saw was a capacity ceiling, not a data problem
nodes.rationale: Before v6, gains in one category traded against losses in another; raising parameters once removed the trade.

nodes.label: The eight phases (evaluation -> scale finale)
nodes.rationale: Each phase changed one thing and was written up separately: evaluation, dataset, fine-tuning, BPE, pretraining, hybrid data, conversation, scale.

nodes.label: Multi-step arithmetic regression 60 -> 54
nodes.rationale: Stage 2 ran 2,500 steps where scratch-trained v2 ran 5,000, and chained computation is the most step-hungry skill in the pool. Phase 6 doubled stage 2 to 5,000 steps on this evidence and multi-step recovered to 64, then 68.

nodes.label: Phase 5 objective — prose before questions
nodes.rationale: v2 could follow formats but not reason: logic 12%, reading 38%. The Phase 4 diagnosis was that the model had never read anything — its entire experience of English was 36,176 templated Q:/A: pairs, so it knew the shape of an answer without the language an answer is made of.

nodes.label: README — Aizen project front door
nodes.rationale: Presents the project as a demonstration of method: every point of benchmark gain came from data, tokenization and method, with the parameter count raised exactly once.

nodes.label: Some regressions are purchases
nodes.rationale: Phase 7 cost 4.25 points overall and bought multi-turn memory; it was approved in advance and reported as a loss rather than smoothed over.

nodes.label: Vocabulary widened 2,048 -> 4,096
nodes.rationale: The domain widened from templated Q&A to open prose, so the tokenizer was retrained on the story corpus; the Phase 4 invariants held — digits stay single tokens and newline never merges.

nodes.label: The 0.8M tiny-shakespeare predecessor (tinygpt.pt)
nodes.rationale: The same architecture at 0.8M parameters on the character-level demo corpus popularised by Karpathy; unrelated to Aizen's weights, which started from random initialisation.

nodes.label: Synthetic task data — computed, never authored
nodes.norm_label: synthetic task data — computed, never authored
nodes.rationale: Every synthetic answer is evaluated in Python rather than typed, so an arithmetic chain cannot be wrong; all generators are deterministic (seed 1337) and regenerable byte-for-byte.

nodes.label: v0 — the original character-level Aizen (14,298,240 params)
nodes.norm_label: v0 — the original character-level aizen (14,298,240 params)
nodes.rationale: 8 layers / 384 dim / 192 context, 73-character vocabulary, trained on exactly one file (data/qa.txt) for 3,000 steps in ~45 minutes on MPS; scored 17.0%, the baseline every later gain is measured from.

nodes.label: AIZEN.md — Complete Model Card & Build Reference
nodes.norm_label: aizen.md — complete model card & build reference
nodes.rationale: Records every data source, licence, token count and hyperparameter so the build is a complete reference rather than a summary.

nodes.label: Karpathy — nanoGPT and 'Let's build GPT'
nodes.rationale: The structural inspiration for this codebase.

nodes.label: What was deliberately not used
nodes.rationale: No web scrape, no Common Crawl, no instruction datasets, no LLM-generated data, no pretrained checkpoint — the from-scratch claim is only meaningful if nothing enters through the data.

nodes.label: Learning order: spelling -> words -> grammar -> format -> facts -> arithmetic
nodes.norm_label: learning order: spelling -> words -> grammar -> format -> facts -> arithmetic
nodes.rationale: v0's val-loss curve is the most instructive artifact in the project because it shows capability arriving in a fixed order.

nodes.label: v0's exact training corpus is no longer reproducible
nodes.norm_label: v0's exact training corpus is no longer reproducible
nodes.rationale: make_qa_data.py was later expanded, so data/qa.txt on disk today (36,176 blocks) is not the 25,390-pair file v0 trained on; the character vocabulary is an exact 73-char match so the checkpoint still loads and scores correctly.

nodes.label: Written from scratch in raw PyTorch
nodes.norm_label: written from scratch in raw pytorch
nodes.rationale: No transformers, no tiktoken, no pretrained weights — architecture, tokenizer, training loops, evaluation harness and web UI all live in the repository and are all readable.

nodes.label: From-scratch byte-pair tokenizer (4,096 vocab)
nodes.rationale: Pair-frequency merging written from scratch with no tiktoken/sentencepiece; 2.64x compression on task data and 4.00x on prose. At identical parameter count BPE moved the benchmark 28.75% -> 35.75% because a character-level model spends capacity learning to spell.

nodes.label: Sennrich et al., 'Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units' (2016)
nodes.norm_label: sennrich et al., 'neural machine translation of rare words with subword units' (2016)

nodes.label: Full printable-ASCII base vocabulary
nodes.rationale: Including all printable ASCII rather than only observed characters is what stopped inference from crashing with KeyError on unusual user input.

nodes.label: Three tokenizer invariants (digits, newline, leading space)
nodes.norm_label: three tokenizer invariants (digits, newline, leading space)
nodes.rationale: Every digit is its own word so arithmetic survives tokenization; newline never merges so the Q:/A: boundary stays visible; leading spaces attach GPT-2 style so ' the' and 'the' are one token each.

nodes.label: bAbI — the curated public task data
nodes.norm_label: babi — the curated public task data
nodes.rationale: Eight task types from the HF mirror Muennighoff/babi (CC BY 3.0); the only curated public task data in the project, used from Phase 6 onward.

nodes.label: Fine-tuning pool lineage (3b + capped bAbI -> 6b -> 7)
nodes.rationale: Verified block by block; aizen_phase6_train.txt (26,400) is marked the over-diluted dead end and v6 descends from the 6b line.

nodes.label: Stage 2 — answer-masked fine-tuning (5,000 steps)
nodes.rationale: Initialised from aizen_phase8_pretrained.pt, 70/30 mixture of aizen_phase7_train.txt with qa.txt, example-aligned windows beginning at a Q:; final masked train 0.0045 / val 0.0142.

nodes.label: Phase 5 stage 2 — 2,500-step fine-tune
nodes.rationale: The Phase 3 recipe applied on top of language knowledge: example-aligned windows, answer-only masking, 70/30 qa.txt with the Phase 3b pool; masked train 0.0165 / val 0.0429.

nodes.label: Weston et al., 'Towards AI-Complete Question Answering' (2015)
nodes.norm_label: weston et al., 'towards ai-complete question answering' (2015)

nodes.label: Answer-only loss masking
nodes.rationale: Masking question and scaffolding tokens is what makes the model an assistant rather than a text completer; masking every A: line in a multi-turn block is how it learned to resolve 'and plus 3?' against its own previous answer.

nodes.label: bAbI dose cap — 300 examples per task (2,400 total)
nodes.norm_label: babi dose cap — 300 examples per task (2,400 total)
nodes.rationale: The same corpus helped at 2,400 examples and hurt at 6,400; at 24% of the pool it crowded out the skills it was meant to support.

nodes.label: Deliberately low stage-2 learning rate (1e-4 -> 1e-5)
nodes.rationale: Stage 2 adapts existing language knowledge to a task rather than learning from zero; a high LR would overwrite the English that 16,000 pretraining steps just bought.

nodes.label: With external data, proportion matters as much as presence
nodes.norm_label: with external data, proportion matters as much as presence
nodes.rationale: The same bAbI corpus helped at 2,400 examples and hurt at 6,400.

nodes.label: Inference server — one Flask app, two models, port 8321
nodes.norm_label: inference server — one flask app, two models, port 8321
nodes.rationale: /chat serves aizen_phase8.pt at temperature 0.5 top-k 20 stopping at newline, /story lazy-loads the pretrained sibling at 0.85/40, /meta returns the model card plus live benchmark data read from results/.

nodes.label: Newest-first multi-turn history packing
nodes.rationale: History is packed into the same Q:/A: format newest-first until the 380-token budget is spent, so context drops from the oldest turn rather than truncating the current question.

nodes.label: Quick start — venv, Flask server on port 8321
nodes.norm_label: quick start — venv, flask server on port 8321
nodes.rationale: torch and flask are the only installs; the server, a terminal client and the scorer are each a single command.

nodes.label: One server, two models, one page (Chat and Story)
nodes.norm_label: one server, two models, one page (chat and story)
nodes.rationale: Chat serves the task-tuned assistant, Story serves the same weights before fine-tuning as pure TinyStories English.

nodes.label: Binding host '::' for Safari's localhost resolution
nodes.norm_label: binding host '::' for safari's localhost resolution
nodes.rationale: Safari resolves localhost to ::1 and cannot reach a server bound only to 127.0.0.1.

nodes.label: Q:/A: prompt formatting at inference
nodes.rationale: The mechanism that turns a text completer into an assistant is prompt formatting and nothing more.
